chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "Then, let them end their tafath". He said: That which occurs from the man during his state of Ihram. When he enters Mecca, he performs the Tawaf and speaks with good speech, for indeed, that is an expiation for that which came from him.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The sacred state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تَفَث: Minor impurities or sins committed during Ihram
key_terms.طَافَ: To perform Tawaf (circumambulation of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'tafath' in the Quranic verse about Hajj and how is it expiated?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets 'tafath' not merely as physical impurities but as minor sins or verbal transgressions incurred during the state of Ihram. The expiation prescribed is the combination of performing Tawaf and engaging in pure, virtuous speech, highlighting the spiritual purification of the pilgrim upon entering the sacred precincts of Mecca. This interpretation underscores the Shia emphasis on the holistic cleansing of both body and soul during Hajj rituals.
